Landed ATS-20 as kit revision 30 in one commit on feat/2026-09-26-automated-tests-sweep. The commit has not been pushed.

**What the runner does now.** When one of the two watch-list tables in RESULTS.md is empty, the runner prints the header row and separator, then a blank line, then `None.`. This covers the functions lizard warned on and the files by layout-§1 band. A table with rows prints no `None.`. The change is a `none_if_empty` helper in testkit/run-automated-tests.sh, called at the end of fn_table and band_table.
- The blank line is needed because GitHub-flavored Markdown would otherwise read `None.` as a row of the table.
- `prior_rows` only reads lines that start with `|`, so `None.` is never carried forward as an entry.
- Revision 25 printed `None.` instead of the header, and revisions 26 to 29 printed the header alone. Printing both is what the AUTOMATED_TESTS.md playbook's Step 3 asks for.

impl.summary:
wow-addon was on master with no sweep item landed, so I cut feat/2026-09-26-automated-tests-sweep from master and committed WA-ATS-01 there (traces ATS-22).

Cause: scripts/bounded_runs.py split the whole command on a regex of `; & | newline ( ) { } $(` and backticks, and paid no attention to quotes. Heredoc body lines and quoted prose (for example `git commit -m "x; lizard is fine"` or `echo "(lua tests/run.lua)"`) became segments of their own and were denied. I reproduced all three before the fix; the installed old hook also blocked my own heredoc commands during this item.

Fix: a small quote- and heredoc-aware Scanner now replaces the regex split and shlex. It handles single and double quotes, escapes and comments. It reads `<<` and `<<-` delimiters, quoted or not, and skips each heredoc body. Heavy runs are still found inside `$(...)` and backticks (also inside double quotes), inside subshells, and in a heredoc fed to a bare shell (`bash <<EOF`). `2>&1` and `&>` are no longer split at the `&`. Leading reserved words (`{ } ! if then elif else while until do`) are skipped, so `if lua tests/run.lua; then` and `{ luacheck .; }` are now refused. Nothing else in the matcher or bounded-runs-hook.sh changed.

Tests: scripts/test_bounded_runs.py went from 16 to 20 cases, all passing. The four new ones cover:
- heredoc bodies are not runs
- quoted prose is not a run
- bare runs are still refused next to prose
- an end-to-end hook-script case: heredoc prose is silent, a bare `lizard -l lua .` is denied

Against the old matcher the four new cases fail and the 16 existing ones pass.

Docs: README.md and CLAUDE.md now say that only command position counts. There is no version bump: no command was added, and the sweep bumps no versions.

The installed plugin copy still runs the old matcher until the plugin is updated and `/reload-plugins` is run.

Your request to add a final `:sync-docs` + `:finalize` step on every touched repo is a change to the workflow script, not to this item. I did not act on it here; it needs your go-ahead to merge to master, per CLAUDE.md. The plan already has WA-ATS-SD for sync-docs in M4.
impl.gate: python3 scripts/test_bounded_runs.py: 20 tests OK (was 16). JSON manifests (plugin.json, marketplace.json, hooks.json) parse. No CR bytes in any changed file (the repo pins LF). No authored file is near 1500 lines (bounded_runs.py is about 370). This repo has no lua, luacheck or lizard gate, per its CLAUDE.md. Tree is clean after the commit; nothing pushed.

issues: Non-blocking: scripts/bounded_runs.py open_heredoc (to_shell only when the heredoc's own segment is a bare shell) means 'cat <<EOF | bash' with a heavy body is no longer denied; master's matcher caught it only by accident, and CLAUDE.md:23 accepts false negatives on exotic shell. A follow-up could treat a heredoc whose pipeline ends in a bare shell as commands.

Note: the installed plugin cache (~/.claude/plugins/cache/wow-addon/wow-addon/2.3.0) still has the old matcher, so the fix reaches sessions only after merge and /reload-plugins. This is expected and does not block.

I ran tests/perf.lua on all 177 commits in 79d4f80..e5bb12c, in a throwaway worktree under the scratchpad, since removed. Nearly all of the rise lands in d0c01f1 (SID-16, the schema v7 category restructure): compile went from 22200 to 42744 B/iter and applyPass from 118147 to 163616. About 1 KB more of applyPass arrives with B8-P7/B8-P7R (Size to fit).

Cause: FC.Compile built categorizedUnion, a copy of every spells-kind category's ids, on every compile. Only the hasUnion gate reads it, and only for a container with a Hide on a unit whose ids are certain (player or pet buffs). SID-16 made the lists bigger, so every compile paid more.

Fix, in /mnt/d/Profile/Users/Tushar/Documents/GIT/AuraMaster/modules/FilterCompiler.lua: the union is now built inside addCategoryGroups, after the R-3 early return and only when FC.IdsAlwaysHonored passes. I also dropped a per-call `cats.union or {}`. Behavior is unchanged: the plan Signature is byte-identical to the pre-change tree across 1280 plans (4 units x 2 aura types x each category hidden or shown alone, with and without spell edits, with and without a whitelist).

Perf, bytes/iter before -> after:
- compile: 42424.0 -> 3576.0
- applyPass: 164883.4 -> 104403.4
- all other scenarios unchanged

- the stale "union computed either way" comments are updated
- docs/performance.md records the bisect
- docs/data-flow.md: two FilterCompiler line citations are corrected (778->790, 950->961) because the edit shifted the lines, and the docs citation test caught it

impl.summary:
I bisected the `recompute` perf rise (6505.88 to 14740.12 bytes/iter, run 20260926-160431). It is not a real regression, so nothing needed fixing and the item landed as a docs commit. The bisect ran tests/perf.lua through ka0s-bounded on all 22 commits in f8729fa..bc284a4, in a throwaway worktree that I have since removed. The rise happens in one step, at b19e9bb (DR-CM-03, the diagnostics report): 3031.9 to 16751.3 bytes/iter. That commit only adds core/Diagnostics.lua, which is not on the recompute path.

Two checks show the figure is a measurement effect:
1. With garbage collection stopped around the same 200-pass loop, a recompute allocates the same amount across the whole range: 226614.5 bytes at f8729fa and 986c51f, 226613.8 at b19e9bb and 226610.6 at bc284a4. Over the same commits the live heap grew from 2408 KB to 2528 KB.
2. At b19e9bb with core/Diagnostics.lua removed from the TOC, `recompute` reads 2619.9, on two runs out of two.

The perf harness reports how much of about 45 MB of garbage is still uncollected when the loop ends. That number shifts whenever the addon loads more code, whatever the recompute itself does. I added a subsection to /mnt/d/Profile/Users/Tushar/Documents/GIT/ConsumableMaster/docs/performance.md that records the bisect, both checks, and how to measure a real allocation change. The file keeps CRLF line endings (182/182). No code changed, tests/perf.lua is untouched, and no exceptions.tsv row was needed.

About your request to add a final sync-docs and finalize step: I couldn't add that from inside this one item. This run only gave me CM-ATS-01 in ConsumableMaster. The step has to be added to the workflow script or the plan by whoever runs the workflow. Per the collection rules, merging and pushing to master also need your explicit go-ahead.
